title: Stored agricultural product pest fumigation management processes

lessons.title: Stored product fumigation at grain sites
lessons.html:
Learning at the silo

In this module you take part in managing fumigations of stored agricultural products in the workplace: maize and wheat in concrete silos and steel bins, bagged grain and seed in warehouses, bunkers, and commodities such as dried fruit, nuts or feed. You work under a registered fumigator and progressively manage parts of the process.

Workplace process

  1. Review monitoring data: insect counts per sample, grain temperatures and moisture.
  2. Confirm the decision to fumigate against the agreed threshold, storage period and buyer requirements.
  3. Assess whether the bin or stack can be sealed; pressure-test where possible.
  4. Plan dose from tonnage or volume, grain temperature and the label, checked by a second person.
  5. Coordinate with the silo manager on bin isolation, intake and outloading schedules, and staff movements.
  6. Prepare: seal, lock out conveyors, set the exclusion zone, post signs, install sampling lines, occupancy check.
  7. Apply, seal and monitor the full exposure, responding to leaks.
  8. Aerate, test headspace and grain, and protect workers during outloading.
  9. Sample after fumigation, incubate and record survivors.
  10. Complete the fumigation record for the client and buyers.

Scenario: harvest pressure

During the busy wheat intake, the silo manager asks whether bin 9 can be fumigated without stopping intake into the neighbouring bins, which share a top conveyor. Your mentor explains that the shared conveyor is a gas escape route and a worker exposure risk. The plan is changed: intake is rerouted to another bank of bins for the exposure period, the shared conveyor is sealed and locked out, and monitoring is placed on the conveyor gallery. Safety decisions sometimes cost time, and the manager is shown why.

lessons.title: Resistance awareness, records and evidence
lessons.html:
Protecting phosphine for the future

Phosphine remains the main tool for stored grain disinfestation. Poor practice in the workplace, such as fumigating leaky bins, shortening exposures or under-dosing, selects for resistant insects. As a future manager, you must insist on good practice every time:

  • Do not fumigate structures that cannot be sealed adequately.
  • Apply the full label dose and full exposure for the grain temperature.
  • Monitor concentrations to prove the fumigation achieved its target.
  • Investigate and report survivors.
  • Support prevention: hygiene, drying, cooling and monitoring, to reduce how often fumigation is needed.

Records buyers and auditors ask for

RecordPurpose
Fumigation log with readingsProof that concentration and time were achieved
Product and registration numberLegal compliance
Clearance readings and timesWorker safety and release of grain
Post-treatment samplingEvidence of efficacy
Operator registrationCompetence

Portfolio evidence

  • Monitoring data and the fumigation decision you helped make.
  • Seal checks, pressure test results and dose calculations.
  • Fumigation logs, clearance records and post-treatment results.
  • Mentor sign-offs and reflections on difficult decisions.

Key points

  • Base fumigation decisions on monitoring data, thresholds and buyer requirements.
  • Coordinate bin isolation and staff movements with the silo manager.
  • Shared conveyors are gas escape routes and must be sealed and locked out.
  • Prevent resistance with good sealing, full doses, full exposures and monitoring.
  • Keep records that prove concentration, time, clearance and efficacy.
